info.title: Smart Water Billing API
info.description: On-premise IoT water billing. Humans authenticate with a JWT from /api/v1/auth/login; meters authenticate per request with the X-Meter-Key header.

post.summary: Exchange credentials for a bearer token
post.description: Returns a JWT carrying the user's role. Admin and Customer are distinguished by the role claim; meters do not log in here — they authenticate per-request with X-Meter-Key.
Admin only. Creates an Admin or Customer account. Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 and never stored or returned in clear.

delete.description: The row is retained with a deletion timestamp so existing invoices stay attributable. Meters held by the user are unassigned rather than deleted, and the email address becomes reusable.

get.description: Admins see every meter. A customer sees only meters assigned to their own account; the filter is applied server-side, not by the caller.

post.description: Admin only. Issues the meter's first ingestion API key in the same response — the only time the plaintext key is ever shown.

put.description: Sets the customer billed for this meter. Passing null unassigns it; already-issued invoices keep the customer they were issued to.

get.description: Returns prefixes and lifecycle timestamps only. Plaintext keys are not recoverable by design.

put.summary: Open or close the supply valve
put.description: Records the DESIRED valve position. The on-site gateway reconciles the physical relay and reports back, so a valve that fails to actuate stays visible instead of being assumed closed.

get.description: Admins may read any meter. A customer may read only meters assigned to their own account; requesting another customer's meter returns 403, not 404, because the meter's existence is not itself a secret.

Derives consumption from the stored reading series rather than a running counter: TOTAL at the last reading on or before the period end, minus TOTAL at the last reading on or before the period start, walked pairwise so a meter reset is summed across. Defaults to the current calendar month. Flags explain any caveat on the figure.
A rolling series for charting. Each month is computed independently with the same formula, so the months sum exactly to the total across the span.

post.description: Authenticated with the per-meter X-Meter-Key header. Idempotent: re-posting a reading for a timestamp that already exists returns 200 with status 'duplicate_ignored' rather than an error, so a device that retries after a timeout is always safe.
For devices that store and forward after a link outage. Each reading is processed independently, so one bad row does not discard the batch; the response reports the outcome of every reading.

get.description: Every plan with its full version history. Versions are immutable, so this is the complete record of what any meter has ever been billed at.

post.description: Creates the plan and publishes its first version. Supports fixed per-unit pricing and slab pricing; slab bands are validated for contiguity by the same domain rules the pricing engine uses.
Closes the current version and opens a successor. Nothing is edited in place, so an invoice issued under the old rates still reprices identically.
Prices a hypothetical consumption against the plan's current version, returning the full band-by-band breakdown. Lets an admin check a tariff before any customer is billed by it.

get.description: Admins see every invoice. A customer sees only their own — the filter is applied server-side and cannot be widened by a query parameter.

get.summary: Get an invoice with its full breakdown
get.description: Returns every line item as stored at generation: band, units, rate and amount. Nothing is recomputed, so the invoice reads the same today as on the day it was issued.

post.description: Records a payment against a mocked provider, with every attempt logged. Idempotent on the caller-supplied key, so a retried checkout cannot charge twice.

Defaults to the previous calendar month. Idempotent: a unique index on (meter_id, period_start) means re-running cannot double-bill, and already-billed meters are reported rather than treated as errors. Meters with no readings are billed the standing charge and flagged, never silently skipped. Pass dryRun to compute and report everything without persisting.

get.summary: Get a billing run with per-meter outcomes

BillingRunResponse.description:
The answer to "did billing work this month?" — per meter, with a reason for every
meter that was not invoiced (ADR-0007).

GenerateInvoicesRequest.description:
Defaults to the previous calendar month, which is what the assignment asks for.
An explicit period is accepted for re-runs and back-fills.

IssuedApiKeyResponse.description:
The plaintext key appears here and nowhere else, ever. It is not stored, cannot
be recovered, and is not written to the audit log — only its prefix is.

PriceQuoteRequest.description: Lets an admin see what a tariff would charge before publishing it.

PublishVersionRequest.description:
Publishing a version never edits the current one — it closes it and opens a
successor, so an invoice issued last month still prices exactly as it did.

ReadingBatchRequest.description: Batch form, for devices that store and forward after a link outage.

anomalies.description: Anomaly flags raised while storing, as readable tokens.

ReadingIngestionResult.description:
What happened to one submitted reading. `Status` is a stable machine token:
`accepted`, `duplicate_ignored`, or `rejected`.

readingAtUtc.description:
When the meter took the reading. Supplied by the device, not the server: a meter
that buffers through a network outage must still report when each reading happened.

flowM3PerHour.description: Instantaneous flow in m3/hr. Optional, diagnostic only.

ReadingRequest.description: A single observation posted by a meter.

Bearer.description: Paste the accessToken returned by POST /api/v1/auth/login.

MeterKey.description: Per-meter ingestion key. Issued when the meter is created and shown only once.
MeterKey.name: X-Meter-Key
